### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff12aed37b35ecf2cc1d8fd9a3f609fa79dfa6e7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d22f921b6a393db376a563ab3c47fbe92374e5df`
Local-runs: none
Scope: no `hits` (`reviewFace` on the five committed paths names no schema and no governed path; the tier is served above the `TIER_DEFAULT` floor because triage 6633820272 sent a permission-baseline widening to contract review) — reviewed whole: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/member-default-explicit-allow.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/member-default-feed-grants.integration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/comment-reaction-own-record-floor.test.ts, .changeset/30108-member-default-feed-grants.md + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/activity-read-visibility.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/parent-record-read-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts (`enforceFeedsCapability`), packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (§5b), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/external-baseline.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/package.json (`exports`), content/docs/ui/pages.mdx, content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx

Inputs: card #30108 (body and all four comments, the ruling 6633054352 included), PR #30222 (body, file list, `git diff origin/main...d22f921b`), the head's check-runs read through the API. Not read as evidence: the dispatch order or the seat's own conclusions; the dev report's measurements were re-derived from the code below.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **What the baseline now grants — exactly the ruling, nothing more.** `member_default.objects` gains `sys_comment: { allowRead, allowCreate, allowEdit: true, allowDelete: false }` and `sys_activity: { allowRead: true, allowCreate/Edit/Delete: false }` (default-permission-sets.ts, the two lines after the new `[#30108]` block). No `allowExport`, `viewAllRecords` or `modifyAllRecords` key on either; no `'*'` entry added (the `[#5491]` NO-WILDCARD note and maintainer ruling of 2026-08-07 in the same object literal still hold, and the pre-existing pin `expect(Object.keys(MEMBER_DEFAULT.objects)).not.toContain('*')` is untouched). ADR-0090 D5 anchor-safety holds: no delete bit anywhere in the set; the new explicit-allow block pins all four of these per object. Correct.
2. **Row access stays derived from the parent record; no row policy is added.** Read side: `installCommentReadVisibility` (comment-access-hooks.ts) is a data middleware on find/findOne/count/aggregate that ANDs `computeThreadVisibilityFilter` into `ctx.ast.where` and, on any failure, ANDs `READ_DENY_ALL` (fails closed); `installActivityReadVisibility` (activity-read-visibility.ts) does the same over `PARENT_GATE_READ_OPS` with `computeParentRecordFilter`, excluding rows that name no parent. Write side: `onInsert` refuses unless `callerCanRead(target)` (`RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`), stamps `author_id` from the session; the `beforeUpdate` hook requires author-or-parent-EDIT and re-checks the new parent on a re-thread. The baseline adds no select/insert policy for either object (pinned: `policiesFor(object,'select'|'insert')` is `[]`), which is right: neither object has a column a `using` predicate could scope by, so a baseline row policy would have replaced the gate's answer with a wrong one. Correct.
3. **The edit limb.** The only update-class policy on `sys_comment` is the wildcard `owner_only_writes` (`created_by == current_user.id`, `positions: ['org_member']`); `sys_comment_moderation` is the delete limb only (`operation: 'delete'`, by the file's own c25b2d52a note). So for an `org_member` an edit reaches the comments they wrote, as the PR claims and block 1 of the integration test measures (`403 PERMISSION_DENIED` on another's comment). One reading to carry: the floor binds `org_member` only; outside that domain (admin sets, which already hold `'*'` edit; an org-less `everyone`-only session) the bound is the comment gate's own author-or-parent-EDIT rule, which is plugin-audit's documented rule and not something this diff widens. Not a must-fix.
4. **External members are not reached — verified in code, and the ruling's premise is wrong, not the implementation.** `resolve-authz-context.ts` §5b: `if (!holdsExternalIdentity(grants.positions) && !grants.positions.includes('everyone')) grants.positions.push('everyone')`; `humanBaselineFor` (external-baseline.ts) returns `[external_default]` for a holder of `org_external` in place of the configured baseline; `external_default` names neither object (pinned in the explicit-allow test). So "`member_default` also reaches `everyone`, including external members" (card risk paragraph, ruling condition 1) is false on `main` and on this head; the condition's intent (the grant widens nothing for externals) is met more strongly than it was written. Reporting this as a corrected premise rather than a fork is right: the grant is not narrowed, option B is not taken, and the external path is measured both ways (baseline-only external refused on both objects; explicit-grant external scoped to its own ticket through the same gates).
5. **The feeds switch and the ruling's "both verbs".** `enforceFeedsCapability` (audit-writers.ts) is registered on `beforeInsert` and `beforeUpdate` for `sys_comment` only, keyed off the `thread_id` target object's `enable.feeds === false`; it has never been registered on a read, and neither `installCommentReadVisibility` nor `commentThreadGate()` consults `enable.feeds`. The PR's statement that reads are not gated by the switch, before or after, is true. Judgment under ③.
6. **Log noise (#23279).** `parent-record-read-gate.ts` asks the security service's `canReadObject` for each parent object before any caller-scoped read of it ("A skipped object is not an access attempt"), so a member's `sys_activity` feed read refuses unreadable parent objects as `$in: []` without logging `[Security] Access denied`. Integration block 5 arms the measurement both ways (a direct refused read logs exactly once; the feed with `canReadObject` withdrawn logs per parent). Holds.
7. **Public accept set / export.** `@objectstack/plugin-security` exports `.` only; no symbol is added (`EXTERNAL_DEFAULT_PERMISSION_SET` already exists on `main`, line 227) and no type, schema, route or `packages/spec` path changes. What changes is the value of the shipped `defaultPermissionSets` constant: a runtime permission behaviour, ruled by the maintainer. `Clause-②: no` is the right declaration and `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. Permission sets merge most-permissively, so an app already naming the two objects (HotCRM) keeps its own bits, delete included; no regression path.
8. **Residual widening to name plainly.** `viewer_readonly` and the admin sets already read both objects through their `'*'` read; after this PR every `org_member` does too. The row set they see is the same gate-derived set. The one observable new reach is item ③.1.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/30108-member-default-feed-grants.md`: `'@objectstack/plugin-security': patch`. The diff publishes no API shape change — a changed default value of a shipped constant, under a maintainer ruling that fixes a declared-not-enforced capability (ADR-0049 shape, as the card frames it). `patch` is consistent with AGENTS.md's "a package whose shipped bytes change takes a patch changeset" and with the fix framing; `minor` was arguable for an access-widening default but is not owed. The `Clause-②:` and `Metadata-protocol:` lines are present and identical in the PR body and the changeset; `Check Changeset` is green on the head. Accepted.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Open question — does "both verbs" allow reads of pre-existing comments on an `enable.feeds: false` object? Ruling: the dev's reading satisfies the condition; it is not a fork.** The condition reads "An object with `enable.feeds: false` still refuses on both verbs" — *still*, i.e. a verification that the switch's existing refusals survive the grant. The switch has refused exactly two verbs since #2707/#10170, create and re-thread, and those are the write verbs this grant opens; both are measured refusing a member with `403 FEEDS_DISABLED` on a record that member reads and edits (integration block 4). It never refused a read, so no refusal was lost, and the documented behaviour (`content/docs/ui/pages.mdx`: the object "suppresses the panel ... and the server refuses comments on such an object") speaks of refusing comments, not of hiding grandfathered rows. Adding a read refusal to the switch would narrow it for every role (`viewer_readonly`, admin sets, every app that grants `sys_comment` today), which the ruling did not order and a PR executing option A must not bundle (Prime Directive #10, no scope expansion). What IS new after this PR: an ordinary member can list a feeds-off object's pre-existing comments through the data API (never through the record page, which suppresses the panel), under the parent gate. That is a residual the maintainer has not ruled on explicitly, not a failed condition. Disposition: dev option B — the lane seat files a separate decision card on the switch ("should `enable.feeds: false` also hide grandfathered comments from readers?") naming this record, and names it in the landing ACCEPT. No hold on this PR; option C (put it to the maintainer before landing) is not warranted because landing changes nothing about that read for any role that already held it.
2. **Reactions.** `member_default` does not name `sys_comment_reaction`; the ruling names two objects and a third would be scope expansion. The record page keeps the reaction control gated on create on `sys_comment_reaction` (plugin-detail.mdx, "A mounted discussion context"). Correct to leave; the dev's dedupe to the open #22566 decision is right, and the gap (members can comment but not react) is a UX residual the card filed there should carry.
3. **The corrected premise of condition 1** (external members) — judged in ①.4: holds; the deviation line is honest and the grant is not narrowed.
4. **Ruling conditions, one by one:** (a) external parent gates hold — yes, and the baseline does not reach externals at all; (b) `enable.feeds: false` still refuses both registered verbs — yes; (c) no #23279 log noise — yes. No fork to report; the grant is the ruling's grant.
5. **Author:** PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay-written); no off-relay author to name.
6. **Governance tier:** the committed file list touches no `GOVERNED_SURFACES` row (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success); this record is the contract review triage owed for a permission-boundary widening, not a Tier S landing key. The PR is a draft with no review and no auto-merge armed.
7. **Checks on `d22f921b`, read through the commits check-runs API:** all 48 runs concluded — 35 `success`, 13 `skipped` (path-filtered UI, docs, dogfood-matrix, opt-in and schedule-gate jobs), 0 failing, 0 in progress — at the last read before this post (all eight `Test Core` shards and `Type Check · workspace` were still in progress at the first read, 02:34Z, and concluded `success` by 02:45Z). Nothing was re-run locally. The PASS below is not conditioned on any check.

### ④ Design judgment

- **default-permission-sets.ts**: the change holds against the code it cites. The new block names the two gates by file and states each one's rule accurately (comment list/read/post on a readable parent; edit author-or-parent-editor under the `owner_only_writes` floor; activity rows served only for readable records, unreadable parent objects skipped through `canReadObject`), names the switch's two verbs correctly, states the anchor rule and the external baseline correctly (§5b, `humanBaselineFor`). The rewritten inbox-pair sentence removes the contradiction the old line 804 would have left ("deliberately NOT included") without erasing why `sys_activity` got no `_self` policy. The set remains explicit-allow and anchor-safe.
- **member-default-explicit-allow.test.ts**: the flipped `sys_activity` negative is replaced by a `_self`-policy pin and a positive block that pins the shape that would quietly widen: no delete/export/view-all/modify-all, no baseline select/insert policy on either object, edit limb exactly `['owner_only_writes']`, `external_default` names neither. That is the right thing to pin at this layer.
- **member-default-feed-grants.integration.test.ts**: drives the real SecurityPlugin, AuditPlugin, SQL driver and the real `resolveAuthzContext` / `assembleExecutionContext` with an app set naming only the app's own objects (the card's `create-objectstack` shape). Blocks 1–5 are the card's scenario (requester on own ticket by row scope; unreadable by row scope and by object; both external cases; feeds-off create and re-thread; the console feed's denial count armed both ways). The technician-with-`viewAllRecords` row of the card's table is not driven, but the gates defer to the parent's read scope (`ReadableIds` leaves), so nothing in this diff decides it differently; not a must-fix.
- **comment-reaction-own-record-floor.test.ts**: header prose only, and the new sentence is accurate (baseline grants read/create/edit; the delete bit stays app-granted).
- **Changeset**: the five bullets restate ①.1–②; the "an app that already grants the two objects keeps working" bullet is the most-permissive-merge fact. No `(narrowing)` arm, correctly.
- No must-fix found. Follow-ups for the lane seat: the ③.1 decision card; the ③.2 residual stays on #22566.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 平台基线 `member_default` 加两行授权：`sys_comment`（读、建、改）和 `sys_activity`（读）；无删除位、无导出、无行策略。
- **为什么改：** 评论和动态在每个对象上默认开启，但没有任何出厂权限集授予这两个对象，新应用的普通成员在自己能看的记录上只看到「没有权限」。您已「同意 A」。
- **风险与回滚：** 能看哪些行仍由父记录门决定；外部成员拿不到这个基线；`enable.feeds: false` 的对象仍拒新评论和挪线程；动态读取不刷拒绝日志。回滚即撤本 PR。
- **先看：** `default-permission-sets.ts` 新增两行及上方注释，再看 `member-default-feed-grants.integration.test.ts`。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run src/member-default-feed-grants.integration.test.ts`，20 条全绿。
- **需要您做的：** 无，席位经合并队列落地（非受管面，620 行）。
- **席位意见：** ACCEPT。三条裁决条件逐条实测成立，契约复审 PASS（6648282410）。一个残留写在下方：关了 feeds 的对象上，关之前留下的旧评论现在普通成员可经 API 读到（页面不显示），这是开关本来就不管读，不是本 PR 收窄或放宽的问题。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:server#2 · head `d22f921b6a393db376a563ab3c47fbe92374e5df`

- **形态:** draft, author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay `pr_create`), no assignee, no review request; 5 files, +607 −13; `check-governed-merges --pr 30222`: NOT governed, 620 lines ≤ 3000. Write tally reported by the dev: 4 writes, `mcp_calls` 0.
- **前提实测:** at `31fe289f` `member_default.objects` named neither object (claim 6646463911 `Premise: holds`); the diff adds exactly the two rows the ruling names. Seat read the diff of `default-permission-sets.ts`, the changeset, and the flipped pins; `owner_only_writes` is the only update-class limb on `sys_comment`; no `'*'`, no `allowDelete`, no export / view-all / modify-all.
- **门禁 check-runs:** 48 runs on the head, 35 `success`, 13 `skipped`, 0 failing. Dev: `dispatch-gates` 60/60, `--ran` 0 NOT-MEASURED, `pnpm lint` green, 8 ablations red-then-restored.
- **契约复审:** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS on this head, comment 6648282410 (served above the path floor because triage 6633820272 sent a permission-baseline widening to review).
- **接受的偏差:** condition 1's premise corrected (the baseline never reaches `org_external`; measured on the real resolver), not a fork. Condition 2 read as the switch's two registered verbs (create, re-thread); the reviewer ruled that reading satisfies "still refuses", and the seat agrees: the switch never gated reads, so no refusal was lost and the grant is not narrowed. Full `pnpm build` ran outside the verify lock (single-agent container).
- **范围外去向:** (1) reads of pre-existing comments on a feeds-off object by a member — Acceptance notes (documented switch behaviour; record page hides the panel; a read refusal would change the switch for every role, which is not this card); (2) `sys_comment_reaction` not in the baseline — carried by the open decision #22566, not filed again; (3) none else. `Skills-docs:` not owed (`Metadata-protocol: none`).
- **落地条款:** `Clause-②: no` (claim line-start key), `Metadata-protocol: none`, changeset `patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-security`. Ordinary queue landing by this seat: `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` on this head.
